title: Daulat Khan Urges Guru Nanak to End Pathan Rule and Take the Throne

blocks.text: Having laid out the facts of his ruin, Daulat Khan places himself in Guru Nanak's refuge and asks for protection against the Pathan order that has devoured its own supporters. The page presents him as a petitioner who now sees truth more clearly than he did while secure in office.

In the boldest part of his plea, Daulat Khan urged Guru Nanak to take the throne of Hindustan so that tyrannical rule might be broken at its root. His request is not merely personal revenge; it is a proposal that spiritual authority should replace failed and violent kingship.

Guru Nanak does not seize that invitation, instead remaining detached from worldly ambition and indicating that he has come to bestow sovereignty, not to hoard it for himself. The page thus closes the appeal by distinguishing divine mission from temporal possession while leaving the political problem fully exposed.
